frequency_question: How often does an emerging market central bank deploy an incremental reserve ratio tool within any given multi-month policy window?
membership_rule: Members are defined as G20 emerging market central banks (e.g., India, Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa) announcing targeted, temporary increases in reserve requirements or incremental reserve ratios on commercial bank deposits. Excluded are standard, routine baseline adjustments to standard cash reserve ratios that occur as part of regular monetary policy normalization cycles.
window: A multi-month policy window of approximately four months duration.

cases.name: RBI incremental cash reserve ratio announcement
RBI incremental cash reserve ratio extension
PBoC reserve requirement ratio targeted cuts/adjustments
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement (macroprudential liquidity buffer) adjustments
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement adjustments

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 5 named (6.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 named hits out of approximately 30 comparable liquidity surplus management windows across major emerging markets; base rate of occurrence is low-to-moderate.
known_gaps: Excludes minor interventions by smaller developing nation central banks due to lack of comparable granular data.
skeleton: Major emerging market central bank discretionary liquidity management episodes over a 20-year span, evaluated across comparable policy windows.
multiplier: 5 relevant targeted liquidity tightening episodes observed across major jurisdictions in comparable windows out of approximately 30 monitored high-liquidity surplus windows.
validity_reason: Central bank toolkits and structural liquidity management approaches evolve slowly over multi-year institutional frameworks.
